title: Add a volume slider to Bandcamp
question: How do I change the volume on Bandcamp's player?
answer: Bandcamp's web player has no volume control: album and track pages only have play, skip and a progress bar, so the only way to turn it down is your computer's volume. The usermods script on this page adds a Volume slider under the player and sets the level of the audio Bandcamp plays. It remembers the level on that artist's pages. Without a userscript, a Bandcamp volume extension or your system volume mixer does the same.
prompt: Add a volume slider to the Bandcamp player.
details:
The slider sits in a new row under the player's progress bar and goes from 0 to 100%. Moving it sets `volume` on the `<audio>` elements Bandcamp uses, and the level is applied again whenever a track starts.

The level is saved in the page's local storage. Each artist has their own `*.bandcamp.com` subdomain, so the saved level is per artist; a new artist starts at 100%. The script runs on album and track pages; it does not change the player in the Bandcamp app, your collection page or Bandcamp Daily. The check loads one album page and moves the slider.

alternatives.title: Bandcamp volume extensions
alternatives.body: Several Chrome extensions, such as Bandcamp Volume, add a slider to the player and do only that.

alternatives.title: System volume mixer
alternatives.body: On Windows the volume mixer can turn down the browser alone. On macOS there is no per-app volume without a third-party tool.

check.actions: const s = document.querySelector('.inline_player input[type=range]'); if (s) { s.value = '30'; s.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true })); }
check.baseline: (() => { const p = document.querySelector('.inline_player'); return !!p && p.checkVisibility() && document.querySelectorAll('audio').length > 0 && !p.querySelector('input[type=range]'); })()
check.expect: (() => { const s = document.querySelector('.inline_player input[type=range]'); const a = [...document.querySelectorAll('audio')]; return !!s && s.checkVisibility() && a.length > 0 && a.every((x) => Math.abs(x.volume - 0.3) < 0.001); })()
